title: CIM-BLAS: Computing-in-Memory Accelerator for BLAS
problem: Basic Linear Algebra Subprograms (BLAS) are foundational for scientific/engineering computing but are data-intensive, bottlenecked by limited memory bandwidth in CPUs and GPUs. Memory bandwidth is the primary constraint for level-1/2 BLAS operations and a significant bottleneck for level-3 operations.
motivation: BLAS is ubiquitous in HPC; memory bandwidth is the critical bottleneck; computing-in-memory can alleviate the memory wall.
method: First CIM accelerator for BLAS based on non-volatile memory (NVM). Features unified floating-point pipeline supporting high-precision arithmetic (to handle BLAS variety). Configurable dataflows support diverse BLAS functions (levels 1, 2, 3). Memory-bound operations execute directly in memory; compute-bound ops leverage PIM's high parallelism.
key_novelty: First CIM-based BLAS accelerator with unified floating-point pipeline and configurable dataflows to support BLAS hierarchy.
contributions: First CIM accelerator for BLAS with high-precision floating-point pipeline
Orders of magnitude performance/energy gains for level-1/2 BLAS
2.6–24.1× energy efficiency improvement for level-3 BLAS; excellent scalability with matrix size

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 2.6–24.1× energy efficiency vs. GPU for level-3 BLAS; orders of magnitude for level-1/2

limitations: Evaluation scope (specific BLAS functions, matrix sizes, NVM technology) not detailed; scalability to modern GPU-optimized BLAS libraries (cuBLAS, MKL); bandwidth-memory tradeoffs for larger matrices not discussed.
primary_theme: CIM-based BLAS acceleration via high-precision unified floating-point pipeline
